candidate_sources.README.md:
# Harbor sonar inspection upload

This workspace selects payload files, starts transfers, records queue and
progress history, and paints progress for its open panel. Runtime: Go 1.13.8.
Dependencies: Go standard library. See src for the session/component entry API.

Selecting a file creates a visit. Retry replaces the physical attempt without
opening another visit. Selecting the same file object again opens a new visit.
The source is shared by attempts and visits for that file. start may emit cached
packets synchronously; decoding yields a full frame, immediately or later.
Decode completion order can differ from packet arrival order.

recordProgress appends transfer history; showProgress paints the open panel.
Queue records, notices, cancellation, retry, navigation, and cleanup retain
their existing behavior. Queue records are {fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}
unless a separate authorization adds byteCount from file.size.

One startup window is relevant to this maintenance request: start may emit
more than one packet synchronously. A showProgress callback may select or hide
another visit before start returns, while its caller has not yet received the
returned cleanup handle.

The same source service also has a diagnostic consumer, Telemetry/
collectProgressTelemetry, whose existing live delta observations are separate
from the panel. Keep its existing behavior during this maintenance.
Removing a listener commits removal before calling the host detach callback;
that callback may synchronously select, hide or dispose. Repeated removal is
inert. Host callbacks execute synchronously unless explicitly deferred.

Files have stable object identity and immutable id/size during these commands.
A full frame replaces displayed state; loaded values can decrease or reset.
A decode result resolves once; rejected decode and physical transfer completion
are outside this embedding's model. Each workspace has its own lifetime.

Environment.call/bind provides a synchronous source embedding: listen(file
 token, callback token) returns a subscription, start can invoke it before
returning, and unlisten may reenter navigation. decode(file token, packet,
completion token) returns {deferred:false,frame} or {deferred:true}. Deferred
completion invokes the bound native closure on an explicit later host turn.
Transport receives a physical cancellation observer corresponding to the
native attempt state; cancel is idempotent. The wire embedding interns file
objects and forwards source/sink calls. Go uses context cancellation; the other
native ports use object flags. No native DOM/Promise runtime is claimed.

checkpoints: A warm panel source delivers cached startup progress, and later packets continue to update the panel.
Complete newer and then older full-frame decodes: both retain their audit effects, while the older frame cannot replace the newer displayed frame.
A later packet with a lower loaded value can replace an earlier frame; numeric magnitude does not determine freshness.
Navigate from showProgress during synchronous startup, then emit another packet before start returns; verify current ownership, cleanup, and subsequent delivery.
Navigate from recordProgress or unlisten; verify that resumed outer work does not paint or replace resources belonging to a newer visit.
Complete previously started decodes after hide, replacement, or disposal; retain audit and suppress retired-visit display.
Retry while cancellation reenters navigation; preserve the accepted retry's original file and visit, record it once, and cancel its resulting transfer if retired.
Verify same-file reopening, repeated cleanup, independent sessions, unchanged queue and notice shapes, and unchanged telemetry observations.
forbidden_effects: Allow an older received full frame to overwrite a newer frame already displayed for the current visit.
Use loaded-value monotonicity to determine frame freshness.
Discard required progress history merely because a frame is stale for display or its visit has closed.
Allow a retired startup to overwrite newer navigation ownership or leave its resources uncanceled.
Add byteCount or otherwise change the queue-record format.
Apply the panel reception or freshness policy to diagnostic telemetry.
lifecycle_identity: File objects have stable identity and immutable id and size.
Each selection creates a distinct visit, including selection of the same file object; retry retains the visit and creates another physical attempt.
Progress audit remains associated with the originating file and attempt; visible publication requires the originating visit to remain current.
Freshness must distinguish packet reception order from decode completion order and must remain valid across synchronous callback reentry.
Each session retains its own lifetime, attempt counters, task collection, and disposal state.

obligations.text: Establish panel reception before invoking start so synchronous cached progress reaches the panel, while preserving subsequent streaming.

Track frame freshness from packet reception rather than decode completion or loaded value. After a newer frame has been published, prevent an older frame from replacing it on the current display, including through reentrant callbacks.

Preserve progress audit for every decode already started, including stale display frames and completion after navigation or disposal. Perform the existing audit before considering visible publication, and recheck current visit authority after callback-capable audit.

Coordinate startup and cancellation so navigation during synchronous startup or cleanup retains newer ownership, retires old resources, and prevents old visits from painting. Reopening the same file must remain functional.

Preserve accepted retry behavior: cancel the prior attempt before enqueueing, retain the entry visit and file across cancellation reentry, record and create the accepted retry, cancel its resulting attempt if its visit ended, and show queued notices only while its visit remains current.
Preserve public APIs, queue and notice payloads, synchronous observable recording order, idempotent cancellation and disposal, ordinary streaming, and the diagnostic consumer's existing behavior.

ordering_barriers: Register the panel listener before start can synchronously emit cached packets.
Capture packet freshness before decoding can complete or invoke host callbacks.
Retain audit before visible publication; check current visit and freshness after audit returns.
Commit display freshness before showProgress can synchronously reenter delivery or navigation.
Remove old visit ownership before callback-capable cancellation; recheck navigation identity before installing a replacement visit.
Make cleanup ownership effective during startup, then reconcile the returned handle without replacing newer ownership.
Keep record before transport and startup, prior-attempt cancellation before retry enqueue, and queued notice after attempt creation and current-visit validation.
preservation: Queue records remain {fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}; notices remain {fileId, attemptId, visitId, status: "queued"}.
Existing progress history is recorded synchronously when immediate decoding completes and on the completion callback for deferred decoding.
Already started decoding remains capable of recording history after listener removal or cancellation.
Cancellation commits context cancellation before listener removal and physical cancellation; repeated cancellation remains inert.
Telemetry retains its existing live delta behavior and its separate subscription and decode path.
A full frame replaces displayed state, including legitimate decreases or resets in loaded values.
scope: Draft contract only; no files modified.
Panel warm-start reception, display freshness, and lifecycle coordination necessary to preserve existing behavior in src/workflow.go.
Normative evidence is the original TASK and supplied public documents and source. Experience and evaluation observations supply no additional requirements.
